[[Image:Rudy Gay 2.jpg|thumb|Rudy Gay doing a pump-dunk, playing for UConn.]] {{Infobox NBA Player | name = Rudy Gay | image = | caption = | position = [[Small forward]] | nickname = | height_ft = 6 | height_in = 9 | weight_lb = 220 | team = | nationality = USA | birth_date = [[August 17]], [[1986]] | birth_place = [[Baltimore, Maryland]] | college = [[University of Connecticut]] | high school = Archbishop Spalding High School | draft_year = 2006 | draft_team = | career_start = | former_teams = | awards = }}'''Rudy Carlton Gay, Jr.''' (born [[August 17]] [[1986]] in [[Baltimore, Maryland]]) is a former [[college basketball]] player for the [[University of Connecticut|UConn Huskies]]. Gay is 6 feet, 9 inches and 220 pounds, and played as a sophomore in the 2005-06 season. ==High School== He was one of the top recruits entering college play after attending Archbishop Spalding High School. Gay was a [[McDonald's All-American]], and a ''[[Parade (magazine)|Parade]]'' First Team All-American in his senior year after averaging a stellar 21.2 points per game, 9.2 rebounds, and 3.7 blocks. [http://www.parade.com/articles/editions/2004/edition_04-04-2004/featured_1 "Meet ''Parade'''s All-America High School Boys Basketball Team"], Michael O'Shea, ''[[Parade (magazine)|Parade]]'', April 4, 2004. ==College== He is often regarded as the most talented player in college basketball. Gay is known for his high-flying dunks and ability to do everything on the court. He was a co-winner (with [[Jeff Green (basketball)|Jeff Green]] of [[Georgetown University]]) of the 2005 [[Big East Conference]] Rookie of the Year award. Rudy was also named the National Freshman of the Year by ''[[The Sporting News]]''. In the [[Summer]] of [[2005]], Rudy was invited to play for the USA's Mens Under 21 World Championship Team. He performed well, posting a double-double while averaging 10.5 points a game and 5.5 rebounds. Before his sophmore season began, Gay was nomminated as BIGEAST Preseason player of the year, along with [[Syracuse]] star, Gerry McNamara. After the season concluded, Gay was one of four division one college players nominated for the Naismith Player of the Year Award (along with [[J.J. Redick]], [[Adam Morrison]], and [[Allan Ray]]). Also, he was an unanimous selection to the BIGEAST's First Team. He tallied his career high in points with 28 vs [[Arkansas]] in the second game of the 2005-2006 season. Gay led the UConn Huskies to a 30-3 record, often the highest scorer, before losing to #11 seed [[George Mason Patriots|George Mason]] in OT, 86-84. ==Draft== Gay, widely regarded as one of the top future NBA prospects, announced on April 17 that he would enter the [[2006 NBA Draft]].[http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/draft2006/news/story?id=2411206 "Gay to leave UConn for NBA draft"], ''[[ESPN|ESPN.com]]'', April 17, 2006. He is expected to be an early [[NBA Draft Lottery|lottery pick]]. He is thought to be lock to be a top 10 draft pick. His draft workouts went well. Rudy has worked out with the [[Toronto Raptors]], who have the 1st pick, [[Chicago Bulls]],(2nd pick),[[Charlotte Bobcats]], (3rd pick) [[Portland Trailblazers]] (4th pick) and the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] (6th pick). These teams, with the exception of Minnesota (where he was exhausted), said that Gay played great and outpreformed the other players he went up against. ==Personal== *Parents: Rudy and Rae Gay *Siblings: Eric, Brett, Yozmin, and Candace ==Statistics== 2003-2004 (High School Senior)
